newsitem.title: USA: Mobil sees Lagoven venture output in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Mobil sees Lagoven venture output in 1999.

text.p: Mobil Corp said initial production of extra-heavy crude under its venture with Venezuela's Lagoven is scheduled to begin in 1999.
Mobil said its Chalmette, La., refinery is expected to process 50,000 barrels per day of the upgraded heavy oil in 1999, increasing to 100,000 barrels daily by 2002.

This production rise coincides with the completion of the Delayed Coker unit at the Jose Industrial Complex on the Venezuelan coast, which will upgrade the eight degree gravity Orinoco crude into a 16 degree gravity synthetic crude oil.
A 50 percent interest in the Chalmette refinery will be part of Mobil's contribution to the venture with Lagoven, spokesman David Dickson said.
Chalmette is a 180,000 barrel per day refinery located in Southeast Louisiana which has conducted two successful test runs of the Cerro Negro crude oil.
Mobil said it and Lagoven currently plan to produce some 1.2 billion barrels of extra-heavy crude oil during the life of the project.
Mobil, at this level of production, will book proved reserves of at least 600 million barrels in the initial years of this project, the company said.
